claims.statement: `createRhAuth({ apiBaseUrl, onError })` initializes the kit's auth store and returns an installable Vue plugin carrying authGuard and publicGuard, and the store checks the session the moment it is created, so any fragment token must be stored before createRhAuth runs.

The `onError` option receives every ApiError from the kit's requests, which is the only client-side place the consents gate can observe a 451 because the store absorbs session-restoration failures with an internal catch.
`useAuth()` exposes reactive `user`, `teams` and `isAuthenticated` for templates and script, with `teams` entries carrying `id.$oid`, `role` and an `active` flag used for team switching in the UI.

`auth.api(path, options?)` is an authenticated fetch wrapper: callers pass a service-relative path, the session is applied on the way out, and any non-2xx response rejects with an ApiError whose `status` is branchable (401 'logged out', 403 ACL, 451 consents).
A plain `fetch` to the same service URL is unauthenticated and answers 401, which the app reads as 'logged out' rather than 'missing bearer token' — the mistake the starter explicitly warns about.
The kit exports the types the app consumes: ApiError, TeamMembership, TeamMember and PendingInvitation, used to type team detail data and view-local refs.

The app uses the kit's full auth method surface: login, register, logout, checkSession, acceptConsents, updateProfile, changePassword, loadTeams, createTeam, switchTeam, listTeamMembers, listInvitations, invite, acceptInvite, activate and getInvitation.

`auth.checkSession()` both restores the session on app start (absorbing failure) and is called explicitly after `acceptConsents()` to reload user and teams, and screens call it on mount to populate profile fields.

`auth.acceptConsents()` performs the acceptance PATCH and triggers a token renewal; the caller then explicitly calls `auth.checkSession()` to reload the session, and the fresh token is mandatory because the server-side guard keeps blocking for the lifetime of the old JWT.
The kit provides `setToken` and `scheduleRefresh` standalone exports for capturing a token delivered in the URL fragment (email verification, OAuth) and arming automatic refresh with the service URL.

Session restoration is deliberately non-blocking: `checkSession` is caught and treated as a signed-out session so the app stays usable, which is why a 451 only becomes visible through the onError hook rather than by failing startup.

Before createRhAuth can be used, the app validates `apiUrl` with the kit's `isValidApiBaseUrl` and mounts only the ConfigPage when it is invalid, because a store created without a service would run session checks against nowhere.
The kit's guards ignore the traditional `next` callback and return their verdict, so the app supplies a no-op `next` and dispatches from `to.meta.guard` in a single global beforeEach.
Reactive kit state is read as bare refs in templates but as `.value` in script (e.g. `auth.user.value?._id`, `auth.teams.value.find(...)`), and UI code must respect that distinction.

The starter consumes @ulabase/kit-vue (pinned to ^0.13.6 in package.json, matching @ulabase/cli ^0.13.6) for all auth behavior: the Vue plugin, useAuth() composable, router guards, authenticated fetch wrapper, and TypeScript types, while the app itself contains no server code.
createRhAuth({ apiBaseUrl, onError }) returns an installable Vue plugin exposing the auth store plus authGuard/publicGuard, and the starter passes consentsOnError as onError.

Bootstrap order is constrained twice: consumeFragmentToken() must run before createRhAuth() because the store checks the session the moment it is created, and the whole auth bootstrap is skipped entirely when isValidApiBaseUrl(environment.apiUrl) fails, mounting a bare ConfigPage with no router or auth store.

Tokens arriving in the URL fragment are applied with the standalone kit exports setToken(accessToken) and scheduleRefresh({ apiBaseUrl }), after which the fragment is scrubbed from the browser URL via history.replaceState.

The app relies on two kit guard behaviors: guards ignore the `next` argument and return a verdict, so main.ts passes a no-op NavigationGuardNext; and guards only run on navigation, so main.ts separately watches rhAuth.store.user to redirect to /auth/login when a user disappears on an auth-guarded route.

The useAuth() surface splits into: session (checkSession, logout), registration/verification (register, verify, activate, forgotPassword, resetPassword), login, invitations (getInvitation, acceptInvite), teams (loadTeams, createTeam, switchTeam, listTeamMembers, invite, removeMember, resendInvite, updateMemberRole, listInvitations, updateTeam, deleteTeam), consents (acceptConsents), profile (updateProfile, changePassword), and raw API access (api).

auth.api(path, options?) applies the session to outgoing requests; callers pass a path rather than an absolute URL, and a plain fetch to the same URL is unauthenticated and answers 401, which reads as logged out rather than a missing header.

Any non-2xx response from auth.api rejects with ApiError ({ status, message }), so app code branches on status codes rather than parsing bodies: 401 for an expired or invalid session, 403 for ACL/permission refusals, 409 for conflicts such as already-a-member, and 451 for the consents gate.

The kit's auth store restores the session as createRhAuth() creates it and swallows the failure (checkSession().catch(() => null)) to keep the app usable, making onError the only observer of why session restoration failed; without it a blocked user and a signed-out user are indistinguishable.

acceptConsents() performs the acceptance PATCH, renews the token with GET /token?renew=true, refreshes /users/me, and updates user (kit >= 0.7.0); the renewal is mandatory because the server-side Guards rule keeps blocking for the lifetime of the old JWT.

Routes declare meta.guard ('auth' or 'public') in routes.ts with children inheriting the shell's guard, and the invitation-acceptance route is deliberately left unguarded so it works signed-out, signed-in, and accountless.

The kit exports the entity types the app types its own state with: ApiError ({ status, message }), TeamMembership ({ id: { $oid }, name, description?, role, active }), TeamMember ({ email, role, joinedAt }), and PendingInvitation ({ email, role, sentAt, expiresAt }).
Account.vue calls checkSession() on mount to read the current user's profile into its form state and disables editing until that call resolves.

TeamDetail.vue reloads team data on the :id route param (not once on mount) because the same component instance is reused, calling loadTeams(), listTeamMembers(), and listInvitations() through the composable; after deleteTeam() it re-loads teams and switches to a remaining one only if none is active.
